best_for: Windows 10 and 11 users who like 7-Zip but want it in the new right-click menu, with dark mode and Zstandard support.

points.title: 7-Zip, fitted to modern Windows
points.text: NanaZip is a 7-Zip fork that adds itself to the Windows 11 context menu, follows dark mode and handles high-DPI screens. Drive menus need Windows 11 22H2 or later.

points.title: More formats than 7-Zip
points.text: It adds Zstandard, Brotli, LZ4 and similar codecs, can read several disk image types plus asar and .NET single-file bundles, and offers extra hashes such as SHA-3 and BLAKE2b.

points.title: Safer extraction by default
points.text: Files pulled from a downloaded archive keep the Mark of the Web, so Windows still warns before running them.

points.title: MSIX only
points.text: The main build ships as an MSIX package, not a classic installer. The portable build is meant for testing and recovery setups, and in it the context menu and file links do not work.

points.title: Needs Windows 10 2004 or later
points.text: Builds are for x64 and Arm64 on Windows 10 version 2004 or Windows Server 2022 and later. There is no Mac or Linux version.

points.title: Free under MIT
points.text: NanaZip costs nothing. The Windows listing keeps 25 versions, and the Microsoft Store also offers a separate Preview channel.
